question.problem:
Solve the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{4}x+2y=-6 \\ -x+\frac{1}{3}y=-10\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
To get rid of fractions, we multiply the first equation by $4$ and the second equation by $3,$ as follows:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{4}x+2y=-6 & |\times 4 \\ -x+\frac{1}{3}y=-10 & |\times 3\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}3x+8y=-24 \\ -3x+y=-30\end{aligned}
$$

We will use the elimination method to solve the system. We can eliminate $x$ by adding the two equations:

$$
\begin{aligned}\cancel{3x}+8y & =-24 \\ -\cancel{3x}+y & =-30 \\ (8y+y) & =(-24-30) \\ 9y & =-54 \\ y & =-6\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $y=-6$ into the first equation to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3x+8y & =-24 \\ 3x+8(-6) & =-24 \\ 3x-48 & =-24 \\ 3x & =24 \\ x & =8\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system is $x=8,\,y=-6.$
